- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show upward momentum or volatility.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced in high-volatility periods (e.g., 2025-05-01, 2024-11-13) — model systematically underestimates upward moves.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward.
- Mean reversion is not captured well — model holds onto overestimated values longer than observed market behavior.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows consistent bias toward higher values, especially when recent history includes strong upward trends.
- Model fails to account for seasonal or event-driven volatility — underestimates spikes in late forecast period (e.g., 2025-05-01, 30d end).
